To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we synthesized new amides of ([1, 2, 4]triazol[1, 5‐c]quinoazolin‐2(3H)‐one‐2‐thiol and investigated their cytotoxicity by bioluminescent inhibition of P. leiognathi and antimicrobial activity.
the compounds 4.21, and 5.1–5.3 are the most active in the bioluminescence assay, and the most active compounds in the antimicrobial activity assay are compounds 4.6–4.8, 5.5, and 6.
the obtained compounds have low antifungal activity and are inactive against Gram‐positive bacteria, but the n‐butylamides 7.1, 7.5 have weak antibacterial activity against Gram‐negative bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of new derivatives of ([1,5‐]triazolo‐2,1,3‐[1,5]triazoloquinazolin‐4‐yl)thio)carbonyl acid amides, which can be considered as a basis for future studies of the structure‐biological activity of these compounds.
the search for new biologically active substances with a wide range of applications.
the development of a new class of antimicrobial compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytotoxicity and antimicrobial activity are dependent on the nature of substituents in the triazoloquinoline ring and on the nature of the carboxylic acid derivative.
the obtained compounds have a moderate cytotoxic activity and low antibacterial and antifungal properties, but their synthesis and biological activity are worthy of further investigation.
compounds 4–6 were more cytotoxic than antimicrobial active, whereas amides 7 were more antimicrobial active than cytotoxic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytotoxicity by bioluminescense inhibition of triazolo‐substituted quinazolines is not a sufficient criterion for their further investigation as potential antimicrobials.
the most promising compounds for further research are the amides of 4‐(4‐chlorophenyl)‐[1,2,5]triazoloquinazoline with n‐butyric, n‐valeric, and n‐capric acids (7.1, 7.5, and 7.9).
the most cytotoxic substances were not the most active antimicrobial agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytotoxic and antimicrobial activity depends on the structure of the substituents in the 4‐position of the quinazoline ring.
the cytotoxicity of the compounds was not correlated with their antimicrobial activity.
the synthesis of triazolo‐quinazolines is a promising method of obtaining new biologically active compounds.
